selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline: cron.allow absent, opsadmin missing, cron active before change
selected_evidence.summary: Initial inspection showing no cron.allow/deny, no opsadmin user, cron.service active
useradd -m opsadmin succeeded, id confirms uid 1000

selected_evidence.requirement: cron.allow created restricting to root and opsadmin
selected_evidence.summary: Wrote /etc/cron.allow with root and opsadmin entries
testuser crontab attempt rejected: 'not allowed to use this program (crontab)'

selected_evidence.requirement: root and opsadmin retain crontab access
selected_evidence.summary: Both opsadmin and root successfully installed and listed a crontab entry

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot id, service, config)
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id cf34dc87-fdca-4c6a-80e1-579d5524a1da, cron active, cron.allow contents
Backgrounded systemctl reboot returned 'reboot_scheduled' before node dropped

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Node unreachable during reboot, then reachable again with new boot_id acf79031-4d4f-41cd-8370-0c3cf9ca7346 (differs from baseline)

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: cron service active, cron.allow persisted, access control still enforced
selected_evidence.summary: cron.service active, /etc/cron.allow intact with root/opsadmin, opsadmin crontab succeeded, new user t2 denied

commands.command: cat /etc/os-release | head -3; echo ---; which cron crontab; systemctl is-active cron; echo ---; ls -la /etc/cron.allow /etc/cron.deny 2>&1; echo ---; id opsadmin 2>&1; echo ---; cat /etc/passwd | grep -E 'root|opsadmin'
